greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα καὶ ἀπηγγέλη τῷ Ιωσηφ ὅτι Ὁ πατήρ σου ἐνοχλεῖται. καὶ ἀναλαβὼν τοὺς δύο υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ, τὸν Μανασση καὶ τὸν Εφραιμ, ἦλθεν πρὸς Ιακωβ.
hint: Joseph hears that his father is ailing and comes to Jacob with his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.

notes.text: ἐνοχλέω is to trouble, disquiet: your father is troubled. The Hebrew has ḥōleh, sick.
He came to Jacob: not in the Hebrew, which ends with the two sons taken along.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[the things which are said|the things which are said and spoken, the words, the sayings, the phrases, the subjects of speech and things, the verbs|ῥῆμα]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] and [[was brought tidings of|was brought tidings of, was reported, was announced, was carried a report of, was related and narrated|ἀπαγγέλλω]] to the [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[the father|the father, the grandfather|πατήρ]] of you [[is troubled|is troubled and disquieted and annoyed, gives trouble or annoyance to, is a nuisance|ἐνοχλέω]]. and [[having taken up|having taken up, having taken into one's hands, having taken on board ship, having taken with one, having taken upon oneself and assumed, having learned by rote, having got back and regained and recovered, having retrieved and made good, having restored and repaired and regained strength and revived, having taken up again and resumed and recollected, having pulled short up and checked and called back, having gained quite over and won over|ἀναλαμβάνω]] the two sons of him, the [[name:Μανασση]] and the [[name:Εφραιμ]], [[came|came, went, went back and returned, was going to and intended, came within a little of and was near|ἔρχομαι]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Ιακωβ]].

names.gloss: (Ιωσηφ, from Hebrew Yôsēp̄, which the Hebrew of 30:24 hears in yōsēp̄, "may he add")
(Μανασση, from Hebrew Mĕnaššeh, which the Hebrew hears in naššanî, "he made me forget")
(Εφραιμ, from Hebrew ʾEprayim, which the Hebrew hears in hiprānî, "he made me fruitful")
(Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")

greek: ἀπηγγέλη δὲ τῷ Ιακωβ λέγοντες Ἰδοὺ ὁ υἱός σου Ιωσηφ ἔρχεται πρὸς σέ. καὶ ἐνισχύσας Ισραηλ ἐκάθισεν ἐπὶ τὴν κλίνην.
hint: Jacob is told that Joseph is coming; Israel gathers his strength and sits up on the bed.

notes.text: A singular passive with a plural participle: it was told him, by those who said it.
On the bed: the Hebrew miṭṭâ, which the Greek of 47:31 read maṭṭeh, staff, from the same consonants.

reading: [[was brought tidings of|was brought tidings of, was reported, was announced, was carried a report of, was related and narrated|ἀπαγγέλλω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], to the [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] the son of you [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[comes|comes, goes, goes back and returns, is going to and intends, comes within a little of and is near|ἔρχομαι]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] you. and [[having strengthened|having strengthened and confirmed, having prevailed in and prevailed among|ἐνισχύω]] [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[made to sit down|made to sit down and seated, set and placed, encamped, set up, sat down and was seated and took his seat, settled and sank in|καθίζω]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[the that on which one lies|the that on which one lies and couch, the bed, the bier|κλίνη]].

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Ιακωβ τῷ Ιωσηφ Ὁ θεός μου ὤφθη μοι ἐν Λουζα ἐν γῇ Χανααν καὶ εὐλόγησέν με
hint: Jacob tells Joseph that his God appeared to him at Luz in Canaan and blessed him.

notes.text: My God. The Hebrew has ʾēl šadday, as at 35:11, where the Greek has ὁ θεός σου.
The aorist passive of ὁράω: was seen by me, appeared to me.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] to the [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] of me [[was seen|was seen, was looked at, was beheld and perceived and observed, was looked out for|ὁράω]] to me [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to [[name:Λουζα]] [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, ground|ἐν; γῆ]] of [[name:Χανααν]] and [[spoke well of|spoke well of, praised, honoured, blessed|εὐλογέω]] me

names.gloss: (Λουζα, from Hebrew Lûz, usually connected with lûz, "almond tree")
(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ εἶπέν μοι Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ αὐξανῶ σε καὶ πληθυνῶ σε καὶ ποιήσω σε εἰς συναγωγὰς ἐθνῶν καὶ δώσω σοι τὴν γῆν ταύτην καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου μετὰ σὲ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αἰώνιον.
hint: God promised to make him many, a gathering of nations, and to give the land to his offspring forever.

notes.text: συναγωγή, a bringing together, for the Hebrew qĕhal ʿammîm, an assembly of peoples; the Greek makes it plural.
A holding lasting for an age, as at 17:8.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to me [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] I [[I will make large|I will make large and increase and augment, I will increase in power and strengthen and exalt and aggrandise, I will promote to honour and glorify and magnify, I will grow and wax and increase, I will grow up|αὐξάνω]] you and [[I will make full|I will make full and increase and multiply|πληθύνω]] you and [[I will make|I will make, I will do, I will produce, I will create|ποιέω]] you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[bringings together|bringings together and unitings, places of assembly and synagogues, drawings together and contractings, formings in column, pursings up, wrinklings, collections, conclusions and inferences|συναγωγή]] [[of numbers of people accustomed to live together|of numbers of people accustomed to live together and companies and bodies of men, of hosts, of swarms and flocks, of nations and peoples, of nations and gentiles, of special classes, of castes and tribes, of sexes|ἔθνος]] and [[I will give|I will give, I will grant, I will provide, I will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to you [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] and [[to the that which is sown|to the that which is sown, to the seed, to the germ and origin and element, to the offspring and issue, to the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of you [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[holding back|holding back and restraining and retention, possession, relation and attitude|κατάσχεσις]] [[lasting for an age|lasting for an age, ever-lasting and eternal|αἰώνιος]].

greek: νῦν οὖν οἱ δύο υἱοί σου οἱ γενόμενοί σοι ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ πρὸ τοῦ με ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἐμοί εἰσιν, Εφραιμ καὶ Μανασση ὡς Ρουβην καὶ Συμεων ἔσονταί μοι·
hint: Jacob claims Joseph's two sons born in Egypt as his own: Ephraim and Manasseh will be to him as Reuben and Simeon.

notes.text: To me they are: the dative of possession, mine.
Ephraim before Manasseh, the younger first, as in the Hebrew, ahead of 48:14.

reading: [[now at this very time|now at this very time, now, of the present, the present time, just now and but now, as it is and as the case now stands, in this case|νῦν]] [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore|οὖν]] the two sons of you [[the ones having come into being|the ones having come to be, the ones having arisen, the ones having been brought into existence|γίνομαι]] to you [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to [[name:Αἰγύπτῳ]] [[before|before, in front of, further on, sooner, rather than|πρό]] [[of the coming|of the coming, of the going, of the going back and returning, of the being going to and intending, of the coming within a little of and being near|ἔρχομαι]] me [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Αἴγυπτον]] to me are, [[name:Εφραιμ]] and [[name:Μανασση]] [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] [[name:Ρουβην]] and [[name:Συμεων]] will be to me;

names.gloss: (Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)
(Ρουβην, from Hebrew Rĕʾûbēn, which the Hebrew of 29:32 hears in rāʾâ bĕʿonyî, "he has seen my affliction")
(Συμεων, from Hebrew Šimʿôn, which the Hebrew of 29:33 hears in šāmaʿ, "he heard")

greek: τὰ δὲ ἔκγονα, ἃ ἐὰν γεννήσῃς μετὰ ταῦτα, σοὶ ἔσονται, ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τῶν ἀδελφῶν αὐτῶν κληθήσονται ἐν τοῖς ἐκείνων κλήροις.
hint: Any children Joseph has after them will be his own and inherit under their brothers' names.

notes.text: Whatever you may beget: the subjunctive with ἐάν, children still to come. The Hebrew has hôladtā, you have begotten.
In those ones' lots: κλῆρος is a lot, then an allotment of land. The Hebrew has bĕnaḥălātām, in their inheritance.

reading: [[the offspring|the offspring, the born of and sprung from|ἔκγονον]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], which ever [[you may beget|you may beget and engender, you may bring forth, you may produce|γεννάω]] [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]], to you will be, [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + dative]] [[to the name|to the name, to the fame, to the mere name, to the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[of the sons of the same mother|of the sons of the same mother, of the brothers, of the near kinsmen|ἀδελφός]] of them [[will be called|will be called, will be summoned, will be invited|καλέω]] [[in the lots|within, inside of, and by means of the lots, the casting lots and drawing lots, the allotments, the pieces of land and portions and farms, the clergy|ἐν; κλῆρος]] [[of those|of those, of the ones there, of the more remote|ἐκεῖνος]].

greek: ἐγὼ δὲ ἡνίκα ἠρχόμην ἐκ Μεσοποταμίας τῆς Συρίας, ἀπέθανεν Ραχηλ ἡ μήτηρ σου ἐν γῇ Χανααν ἐγγίζοντός μου κατὰ τὸν ἱππόδρομον χαβραθα τῆς γῆς τοῦ ἐλθεῖν Εφραθα, καὶ κατώρυξα αὐτὴν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ ἱπποδρόμου (αὕτη ἐστὶν Βαιθλεεμ). —
hint: Jacob recalls that Rachel died on the road near Ephrath when he came from Mesopotamia, and that he buried her there.

notes.text: Your mother. The Hebrew has ʿālay, upon me, to my sorrow.
By the racecourse, chabratha: the Hebrew kibrat-ʾereṣ, a stretch of land, kept untranslated as at 35:16, with ἱππόδρομος beside it, a course's length as a measure of distance.
On the road of the racecourse. The Hebrew has bĕderek ʾeprāt, on the way to Ephrath.
So Rahlfs spells it here, where 35:19 has Βηθλεεμ; his apparatus marks the spelling as his own.

reading: I [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[at which time|at which time and when, since, whenever|ἡνίκα]] [[I was coming|I was coming, I was going, I was going back and returning, I was going to and intending, I was coming within a little of and being near|ἔρχομαι]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of [[name:Μεσοποταμίας]] of the [[name:Συρίας]], [[died off|died off and died, was put to death and slain|ἀποθνήσκω]] [[name:Ραχηλ]] [[the mother|the mother, the dam, the source|μήτηρ]] of you [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, ground|ἐν; γῆ]] of [[name:Χανααν]] [[of bringing near|of bringing near and bringing up to, of approaching, of being imminent, of approximating to, of being next of kin, of being on the point of|ἐγγίζω]] of me [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[the chariot-road|the chariot-road, the race-course|ἱππόδρομος]] [[name:χαβραθα]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]] [[of the coming|of the coming, of the going, of the going back and returning, of the being going to and intending, of the coming within a little of and being near|ἔρχομαι]] [[name:Εφραθα]], and [[I buried in the earth|I buried in the earth, I buried|κατορύσσω]] her [[in the way|within, inside of, and by means of the way, the path, the track, the road, the highway, the course, the journey, the manner and method|ἐν; ὁδός]] [[of the chariot-road|of the chariot-road, of the race-course|ἱππόδρομος]] ([[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] is [[name:Βαιθλεεμ]]).

names.gloss: (Μεσοποταμία, Greek, "the land between the rivers", for Hebrew Paddān, as for Paddan-ʾĂrām elsewhere)
(Συρία, the Greek name of the land, Hebrew ʾĂrām; the Hebrew here has Paddān alone)
(Ραχηλ, from Hebrew Rāḥēl, "ewe")
(χαβραθα, the Hebrew kibrat left untranslated, a stretch of ground of unknown length)
(Εφραθα, from Hebrew ʾEprātâ, usually connected with pārâ, "to be fruitful")
(Βαιθλεεμ, from Hebrew Bêt-Leḥem, "house of bread")

greek: ἰδὼν δὲ Ισραηλ τοὺς υἱοὺς Ιωσηφ εἶπεν Τίνες σοι οὗτοι;
hint: Israel sees Joseph's sons and asks who they are.

notes.text: A verbless question: who to you these? The dative of possession again, whose are these.

reading: [[having seen|having seen, having perceived, having beheld, having looked at|ὁράω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ισραηλ]] the sons of [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] who to you [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]]?

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Ιωσηφ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ Υἱοί μού εἰσιν, οὓς ἔδωκέν μοι ὁ θεὸς ἐνταῦθα. καὶ εἶπεν Ιακωβ Προσάγαγέ μοι αὐτούς, ἵνα εὐλογήσω αὐτούς.
hint: Joseph says these are the sons God gave him in Egypt; Jacob asks for them to be brought, to bless them.

notes.text: Here, in Egypt: the Hebrew bāzeh, in this place.
The aorist subjunctive after ἵνα: that I may bless them.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[to the father|to the father, to the grandfather|πατήρ]] of him sons of me are, whom [[gave|gave, granted, provided, gave over and delivered up|δίδωμι]] to me [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[here|here, there, hither and thither, at the very time and then, herein, in this state of things and in this position|ἐνταῦθα]]. and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[bring to|bring to, furnish and supply, put to and add, move towards and apply|προσάγω]] to me them, [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] [[I may speak well of|I may speak well of, I may praise, I may honour, I may bless|εὐλογέω]] them.

greek: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ Ισραηλ ἐβαρυώπησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ γήρους, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο βλέπειν· καὶ ἤγγισεν αὐτοὺς πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐφίλησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ περιέλαβεν αὐτούς.
hint: Israel's eyes have grown dim with age; Joseph brings the boys near, and he kisses and embraces them.

notes.text: βαρυωπέω, to be dim-sighted, one word for the Hebrew kābĕdû, the eyes were heavy. LSJ cites this verse; Middle Liddell lacks the word.
φιλέω, the word of affection, to love, to treat affectionately, where the Hebrew has wayyiššaq, he kissed.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the eyes|the eyes, the dearest and best, the comfort, the buds|ὀφθαλμός]] of [[name:Ισραηλ]] were dim-sighted [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] of the old age, and not [[was being able|was being able and capable and strong enough, was powerful and mighty, was having influence, was daring and bearing, was passing for, was worth, was equivalent to, was signifying and meaning, was availing|δύναμαι]] [[to see|to see and have the power of sight, to look, to look longingly and expect eagerly, to look to, to beware of, to see that, to see and behold, to see the light of day and live, to be alive and live|βλέπω]]; and [[brought near|brought near and brought up to, approached, was imminent, approximated to, was next of kin, was on the point of|ἐγγίζω]] them [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] him, and [[loved|loved, regarded with affection, felt affection, loved and cherished, treated affectionately and kindly and welcomed|φιλέω]] them and [[seized around|seized around and embraced, encompassed and surrounded, intercepted, got hold of and caught, comprehended and included|περιλαμβάνω]] them.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Ισραηλ πρὸς Ιωσηφ Ἰδοὺ τοῦ προσώπου σου οὐκ ἐστερήθην, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔδειξέν μοι ὁ θεὸς καὶ τὸ σπέρμα σου.
hint: Israel says he never thought to keep Joseph's face, yet God has shown him Joseph's offspring too.

notes.text: I was not deprived of your face. The Hebrew has rĕʾōh pāneykā lōʾ pillāltî, I had not thought to see your face.
καί as an adverb: your offspring also.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[of the face|of the face and visage and countenance, of the look, of the mask, of the outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] of you not [[I was deprived|I was deprived, I was bereaved, I was robbed of, I was taken away|στερέω]], and [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[brought to light|brought to light and displayed and exhibited, set before one, showed and pointed out, told and explained and taught, showed and proved, informed against, offered and proffered, caused, welcomed and greeted and pledged|δείκνυμι]] to me [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[also|also and even, but, nay, and yet, as, likewise|καί]] [[the that which is sown|the that which is sown, the seed, the germ and origin and element, the offspring and issue, the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of you.

greek: καὶ ἐξήγαγεν Ιωσηφ αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν γονάτων αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: Joseph takes the boys from Israel's knees, and they bow down before him with their faces to the ground.

notes.text: They bowed to him, the boys to Jacob. The Hebrew has the singular, wayyištaḥû, Joseph bowing.

reading: and [[led out|led out, led and carried out from, brought forth into the world, marched out, ejected, carried out and exported, drew off, called forth and excited, led on and tempted|ἐξάγω]] [[name:Ιωσηφ]] them [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the knees|of the knees, of the laps, of the joints|γόνυ]] of him, and [[made obeisance|made obeisance, fell down and worshipped and worshipped and adored, did reverence to, made the salam, prostrated themselves before|προσκυνέω]] to him [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[face|face and visage and countenance, look, mask, outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]].

greek: λαβὼν δὲ Ιωσηφ τοὺς δύο υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ, τόν τε Εφραιμ ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ ἐξ ἀριστερῶν δὲ Ισραηλ, τὸν δὲ Μανασση ἐν τῇ ἀριστερᾷ ἐκ δεξιῶν δὲ Ισραηλ, ἤγγισεν αὐτοὺς αὐτῷ.
hint: Joseph sets Ephraim at Israel's left and Manasseh at his right, and brings them near.

notes.lemma: ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ ἐξ ἀριστερῶν δὲ Ισραηλ
notes.text: In his right hand, and so on Israel's left: δεξιός and ἀριστερός used as nouns, the hand understood.

reading: [[having taken|having taken, having received, having taken hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιωσηφ]] the two sons of him, [[and|and, both and, and also|τε]] the [[name:Εφραιμ]] [[in the right|within, inside of, and by means of the right, the on the right hand, the fortunate and boding good and lucky, the dexterous and ready, the sharp and shrewd and clever|ἐν; δεξιός]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of left|of left and on the left, of left hand, of boding ill and ominous|ἀριστερός]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], of [[name:Ισραηλ]], [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], the [[name:Μανασση]] [[in the left|within, inside of, and by means of the left and on the left, the left hand, the boding ill and ominous|ἐν; ἀριστερός]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of right|of right, of on the right hand, of fortunate and boding good and lucky, of dexterous and ready, of sharp and shrewd and clever|δεξιός]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], of [[name:Ισραηλ]], [[brought near|brought near and brought up to, approached, was imminent, approximated to, was next of kin, was on the point of|ἐγγίζω]] them to him.

greek: ἐκτείνας δὲ Ισραηλ τὴν χεῖρα τὴν δεξιὰν ἐπέβαλεν ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν Εφραιμ — οὗτος δὲ ἦν ὁ νεώτερος — καὶ τὴν ἀριστερὰν ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν Μανασση, ἐναλλὰξ τὰς χεῖρας.
hint: Israel crosses his hands, putting his right on Ephraim, the younger, and his left on Manasseh.

notes.text: The hands crosswise. The Hebrew has śikkēl ʾet-yādāyw, which is read as he crossed his hands or as he guided them wittingly; the Greek takes the first.
An aside, set off by Rahlfs's dashes: and he was the younger.

greek: καὶ ηὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ εἶπεν Ὁ θεός, ᾧ εὐηρέστησαν οἱ πατέρες μου ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ Αβρααμ καὶ Ισαακ, ὁ θεὸς ὁ τρέφων με ἐκ νεότητος ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης,
hint: Israel blesses them by the God before whom Abraham and Isaac walked, who has fed him all his life.

notes.text: He blessed them. The Hebrew has wayĕbārek ʾet-yôsēp, he blessed Joseph.
To whom they were well pleasing, εὐαρεστέω, as at 5:22 and 6:9. The Hebrew has hithallĕkû, walked before.
τρέφω, first to thicken, then to rear and feed. The Hebrew has hārōʿeh ʾōtî, who shepherded me.

greek: ὁ ἄγγελος ὁ ῥυόμενός με ἐκ πάντων τῶν κακῶν εὐλογήσαι τὰ παιδία ταῦτα, καὶ ἐπικληθήσεται ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸ ὄνομά μου καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῶν πατέρων μου Αβρααμ καὶ Ισαακ, καὶ πληθυνθείησαν εἰς πλῆθος πολὺ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: Israel prays that the angel who rescued him bless the boys, and that his name and his fathers' live on in them.

notes.text: ῥύομαι, to draw to oneself, to rescue, for the Hebrew hagōʾēl, the redeemer: the angel who rescues.
Two aorist optatives, the mood of a wish: may he bless, may they be multiplied.
May they be multiplied into a great multitude. The Hebrew has wĕyidgû lārōb, from dāg, fish: may they teem.

hint: Joseph is displeased that his father's right hand is on Ephraim and tries to move it to Manasseh.

notes.text: It appeared heavy to him: καταφαίνω in the passive, to become visible, to be plain. The Hebrew has wayyēraʿ bĕʿênāyw, it was evil in his eyes.
The middle of ἀντιλαμβάνω, to lay hold of, with the genitive of what is held.

hint: Joseph tells his father the other is the firstborn and asks him to put his right hand on Manasseh.

notes.text: The vocative: father.

greek: καὶ οὐκ ἠθέλησεν, ἀλλὰ εἶπεν Οἶδα, τέκνον, οἶδα· καὶ οὗτος ἔσται εἰς λαόν, καὶ οὗτος ὑψωθήσεται, ἀλλὰ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ νεώτερος μείζων αὐτοῦ ἔσται, καὶ τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ ἔσται εἰς πλῆθος ἐθνῶν.
hint: Israel refuses: Manasseh too will become a people, but his younger brother will be greater, his seed many nations.

notes.text: καί as an adverb both times, he also, for the Hebrew gam-hûʾ … wĕgam-hûʾ.
The comparative of μέγας with the genitive of comparison: bigger than he.
Into a multitude of nations, for the Hebrew mĕlōʾ-haggôyim, the fullness of the nations.

greek: καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ λέγων Ἐν ὑμῖν εὐλογηθήσεται Ισραηλ λέγοντες Ποιήσαι σε ὁ θεὸς ὡς Εφραιμ καὶ ὡς Μανασση· καὶ ἔθηκεν τὸν Εφραιμ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Μανασση. —
hint: Israel blesses the boys that day with a blessing formula naming Ephraim and Manasseh, and sets Ephraim first.

notes.text: In you, plural, Israel will be blessed, the passive. The Hebrew has bĕkā yĕbārēk yiśrāʾēl, by you, singular, Israel will bless.
The aorist optative of ποιέω, a wish: may God make you.

hint: Israel tells Joseph he is dying, but God will be with them and bring them back to their fathers' land.

notes.text: Plural throughout: Joseph and his house, though he alone is spoken to.

greek: ἐγὼ δὲ δίδωμί σοι Σικιμα ἐξαίρετον ὑπὲρ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου, ἣν ἔλαβον ἐκ χειρὸς Αμορραίων ἐν μαχαίρᾳ μου καὶ τόξῳ.
hint: Jacob gives Joseph Shechem as a choice portion above his brothers, taken from the Amorites by sword and bow.

notes.text: Shechem, chosen. The Hebrew has šĕkem ʾaḥad, one shoulder, a portion, the word that is also the city's name; the Greek reads the city. John 4:5 places Jacob's gift to Joseph near Sychar.
ὑπέρ with the accusative, over and beyond: above your brothers.
ἥν, feminine singular, takes Σικιμα as one place, which elsewhere the Greek declines as a neuter plural, Σικιμων, Σικιμοις.
